newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Regent says JV to launch mutual fund in Russia.
newsitem.headline: Regent says JV to launch mutual fund in Russia.

text.p: Regent Pacific Group Ltd said it will form a joint venture with one of Russia's top five banks and two other partners to launch a group of mutual funds in Russia early next year.
"Over five years we estimate the potential (mutual funds) market in Russia at between US$20 billion and US$50 billion," managing director James Mellon told Reuters in an interview.
Nobody has established a mutual fund market presence in Russia, even though Russians have an average savings rate in excess of 40 percent, Mellon said.

Existing markets in the United States, Europe and Hong Kong are already "well picked-over" and Regent Pacific, a fund management firm founded only six years ago, could not compete with existing players' distribution networks, Mellon said.
But in Russia, nobody has yet established distribution networks and there is, as yet, no foreign competition.
"No one is in there," he said.
Regent will announce in two weeks the name of one of Russia's five biggest banks as a joint venture partner in a new fund management company, which will be launched early next year.
The joint venture will also include two other unidentified partners to establish the sort of "high volumes systems required," Mellon said.

Regent Pacific is already the largest foreign portfolio investor in Russia with US$500 million invested in the soaring Moscow stock market through a subsidiary broker, which commands 20 percent of Russia's fledgling broking industry, Mellon said.
